messages.subject: Reparameterizing a mixture
parts:
Hey all,

I'm trying to reparameterize my beast of a model, but I had a much less intimidating question.

I'm trying to define a mixture for a prior, something like:



Now, I don't want to sample from a .01, because it slows everything else down.

Currently, I have, e.g., (not actual code from model, but conceptually):

target += log_sum_exp(log1m(pi) + normal_lpdf(alpha | beta, .01) , log(pi) + normal_lpdf(alpha | beta, 1);

Is there a simple way of doing the above, but doing so on a unit scale? Intuitively, I thought I could do ... normal_lpdf(alpha*100 | beta, 1), but it leads to a very different estimate altogether for reasons I don't understand.

messages.author: f769d7d2cfcf4edc
messages.subject: Re: Reparameterizing a mixture
parts:
I think I derived it.



So you could use normal_lpdf(alpha | beta, 1), but add the above quantity to the log posterior target for that component, where sigma_2 is 1 and sigma_1 is .01.

No idea if this will actually help speed up sampling, but that *is* the conversion from one scale to another.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Reparameterizing a mixture
parts:
> On Dec 8, 2016, at 8:18 PM, Stephen Martin <hwki...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> ...

>
> target += log_sum_exp(log1m(pi) + normal_lpdf(alpha | beta, .01) , log(pi) + normal_lpdf(alpha | beta, 1);
>
> Is there a simple way of doing the above, but doing so on a unit scale? Intuitively, I thought I could do ... normal_lpdf(alpha*100 | beta, 1), but it leads to a very different estimate altogether for reasons I don't understand.

Because it's not the same density. Just write out the log density
up to a propirtion: look at the kernel:

0.5 * ((alpha * 100 - mu) / 1)^2 != 0.5 * ((alpha - mu) / .01)^2

We typically recommend the Cauchy distribution if you want to concentrate
most of the mass around a point but allow for long tails. It's got
better continuity and differentiability properties than this kind of
mixture.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Reparameterizing a mixture
parts:
The goal of the model was to test another parameterization I've seen in paper. They purposefully have one prior with a spiked dsitribution and another that isn't. The idea is to choose between the priors.

Specifically, it either allows two parameters to be essentially equivalent (spiked prior) or to be different (non-spiked prior).

I couldn't find an easy way of speeding it up because ultimately the posterior will have a spike somewhere, so I think I'm giving up on it. Ran a little longer than my current method and provided less accurate inferences.
